mechanism_finding: C produced a strict feedback-conditioned repair: its first clean replay passed the public goal but failed frozen provenance qualification, the same Agent session replaced uv's seeded virtual environment with native python -m venv, and the revised exact program passed clean replay and Official EnvBench.
effect_finding: All three arms passed Official EnvBench. The retryable loop therefore produced no Official Pass@1 advantage on this case.
boundary_interpretation: C repaired unowned files introduced by uv venv --seed, not a project dependency or an Official missing-import failure. This is valid mechanism evidence under boundary v5 but cannot support a benchmark-success claim.
benchmark_validity_finding: B passed the frozen missing-import metric while pip reported absent transitive dependencies. Official EnvBench success must therefore be reported separately from complete runnable deployment.
path_quality_observation: The independent Agents selected materially different paths before replay feedback: B minimized the measured goal, C built a complete CPU environment, and A built a complete default PyTorch environment with large CUDA dependencies. C was descriptively fastest, but this stochastic single-case ordering is not a causal treatment effect.
resource_observation: Package resolution and binary transfer dominated wall time and network traffic. Construction and Official evaluation used distinct cache boundaries, so large artifacts were transferred repeatedly.
